headline: Highest risk is data leakage from kotaemon’s broad network/API access into whisper’s local audio-only workflow; prompt-injection and capability-conflict are limited by the lack of shared channels.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon exposes web UI and file-backed RAG workflows, but whisper has no clipboard, filesystem read, MCP, or browser surface to ingest kotaemon output by default. The pair lacks a documented shared communication channel, so a prompt-injection bridge is not evidenced. Uncertainty is low because whisper’s I/O is narrowly audio-file based.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies kotaemon text into a downstream prompt that whisper parses, the pathway becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not pipe kotaemon text into any instruction parser.
Disable any manual copy-paste workflow between agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags if a shared queue is introduced.

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document classes and can call external APIs; whisper is local-only with no network egress. If they share files or a workspace, sensitive kotaemon inputs could be exposed to whisper’s audio-file processing path or vice versa through operator handling. The interaction is indirect, but the sensitive-data blast radius is real.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace directory, leakage risk increases.
IF kotaemon is configured to send document contents to third-party APIs, sensitive data leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories for documents and audio.
Remove API keys from any shared test corpus.
Restrict kotaemon to non-sensitive sample data.
Confirm whisper only processes local audio files.
requires-engineering: add per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon supports multiple instances and writes to ./ktem_app_data, while whisper cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Any conflict would require an unusual shared directory or external orchestrator, so the blast radius is small and the pathway is not default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file contention can occur.
IF an external orchestrator serializes neither agent, race conditions may appear.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run only one kotaemon instance per workspace.
Avoid sharing git working trees.
Check for file-lock support before concurrent runs.

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces document-grounded answers and citations, and whisper can emit transcripts from audio. If one agent’s output is fed into the other without verification, errors can cascade into downstream summaries or actions. Whisper is not an action agent, so this is not high, but the default trust chain can still propagate mistakes.
conditions: IF kotaemon output is used as authoritative source text for a later workflow, errors can propagate.
IF whisper transcripts are treated as ground truth without human review, transcription mistakes cascade.
mitigations: Require human review of both outputs.
Keep source documents and transcripts side by side.
Add a verification step before any downstream action.
Flag low-confidence transcript segments for review.

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon handles API keys and document classes that may include regulated content, while whisper handles audio/speech only. If the same regulated data class is transcribed or indexed across both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show certifications or residency controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF regulated audio or documents are processed by both agents, retention policy mismatch becomes relevant.
IF deployment policy requires specific residency or certification controls, the profiles do not evidence them.
mitigations: Classify the data before processing.
Keep regulated audio out of kotaemon workflows.
Document retention for transcripts and documents separately.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to deployment.
